```data
orchestrator/decision_log.py:164 explain() pairs a decision with every later outcome matching (subject, kind) instead of stopping at the next decision of that same kind. For subjects/kinds that recur (e.g. repeated 'routing' re-tries, or per-tick 'capacity'/'concurrency'/'wave' decisions for the same goal), every earlier decision ends up with outcomes that actually belong to a later decision, corrupting the audit trail this module exists to provide. Only the single-decision acceptance test is covered, so this slips through; needs the outcome-scan bounded by the index of the next same-kind decision for that subject.
```

result.summary: The round-2 fix does not address the review comment from round 1. git log shows only one commit (4926769) ever touched orchestrator/decision_log.py — no follow-up commit changed the explain() logic. Reproduced the exact corruption described in the original rejection: two same-kind decisions for one subject plus a single later outcome results in that outcome being attached to both decisions instead of only the nearer one. Requesting changes again on the same finding.

comments.issue: explain() still pairs a decision with every later outcome matching (subject, kind) instead of stopping at the next decision of that same kind — the exact bug from the prior rejection round is unchanged. Verified by reproducing it: recording two 'routing' decisions for the same subject followed by one outcome row causes the outcome to appear under BOTH decisions' `outcomes` list, when it should only belong to the more recent one (r2). Only the single-decision case is covered by test_explain_pairs_decisions_with_later_outcomes, so this slips through. Needs the outcome scan in explain() bounded to rows between `index` and the index of the next row with the same subject+kind that is itself a decision (not an outcome).
